description: Hi everyone! I’m a Computer Science student deeply passionate about the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Quantum Computing. I love exploring how quantum mechanics can supercharge computational models and solve complex real-world problems that classical systems struggle with.
summary:
During severe floods and wildfires, dense cloud decks and heavy smoke plumes blind conventional optical Earth-observation satellites (like Landsat and Sentinel-2), leaving emergency coordinators with zero situational awareness during the first critical 72 hours. Q-SAR Sentinel 2.0 addresses the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge by harnessing all-weather, day-and-night Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery to penetrate persistent weather barriers and restore ground visibility.

I developed an operational, end-to-end mission control platform that ingests pre- and post-disaster SAR backscatter from Copernicus Sentinel-1 (C-band) and NASA-ISRO SAR (NISAR L-band simulation) to automatically isolate flood inundation, canopy burn scars, and crop stress. The platform pairs a hybrid quantum-classical neural classifier (HybridQSARNet) with constraint-preserving XY-QAOA quantum corridor routing over OpenStreetMap infrastructure networks. It equips first responders with verified hazard perimeters, ranked chokepoints, human-in-the-loop triage, and mission-tailored evacuation routes for drones, rescue vehicles, and medical convoys.
details:
Q-SAR Sentinel 2.0: Bi-Temporal SAR Disaster Assessment & Quantum Emergency Routing

Q-SAR Sentinel 2.0 is an interactive tactical decision-support dashboard built for disaster response commanders and field rescue personnel. Operating seamlessly through severe cloud cover, heavy rain, and wildfire smoke, the platform automatically detects surface water inundation and wildfire destruction, cross-references damage against OpenStreetMap vector infrastructure, flags uncertain detections for human operator triage, and solves multi-objective emergency routing problems using quantum optimization.

How It Works: The 5-Stage Analytical Pipeline

The platform executes an end-to-end analytical pipeline to transform raw satellite radar data into actionable field intelligence:

  1. Dual-Sensor Bi-Temporal Radar Physics

    • Ingests co-registered pre- and post-event Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) scenes (Sentinel-1 C-band VV/VH and simulated NISAR L-band HH/HV).
    • Isolates distinct physical scattering signatures: specular reflection from open water (-6 to -12 dB drop), corner-reflector "double-bounce" from flooded vegetation (+3 to +5 dB rise), and volume scattering loss from destroyed forest canopies.
    • Utilizes a compact deep learning framework integrating a dual-branch classical feature extractor (spatial and intensity-based image analysis) with a parameterized quantum circuit for complex pattern recognition.
    • Incorporates a built-in uncertainty mechanism that flags ambiguous or low-confidence inputs for human review rather than forcing unreliable predictions in high-stakes environments.
    • Calculates cosine-latitude geodesic damage areas ($\text{km}^2$ and hectares) and overlays flooded bridges, isolated settlements, and critical emergency facilities (hospitals, clinics, police, and fire stations).
    • Generates a ranked priority verification queue to guide commander attention.
    • Formulates local road networks as a quantum optimization problem to identify optimal evacuation corridors, ensuring nearly all generated solutions remain strictly valid and feasible.
      • Low Risk Aversion (Drone Reconnaissance): Prioritizes the shortest, fastest path for rapid aerial surveillance.
      • Moderate Risk Aversion (Rescue Vehicles): Balances speed and safety to bypass severe obstacles like deeply flooded roads.
      • High Risk Aversion (Medical Evacuation): Enforces maximum-safety detours that steer entirely clear of active hazard zones and compromised infrastructure.
    • Produces one-click downloadable GeoJSON corridor files compatible with ATAK, QGIS, and field GPS units, alongside printable official Situation Reports (SITREPs).

Key Benefits

  • Zero Weather Delay: Responders obtain verified damage assessments immediately without waiting 24–72 hours for optical satellite cloud cover to clear.
  • Trustworthy Human-in-the-Loop AI: Unambiguous damage is processed automatically, while high-uncertainty areas are surfaced directly to human commanders for verification and sign-off.
  • Infrastructure-Aware Routing: Prevents relief convoys from wasting critical time or risking lives by turning into dead-end submerged bridges or burning roads.

Project Vision & Impact

Our goal is to operationalize spaceborne SAR data into an accessible, real-time command tool for global civil defense organizations—reducing emergency response latency from days to minutes and saving lives during sudden flood and wildfire disasters.
